Which of the following BEST describes why self-learning AI systems can suffer from the test oracle problem?

- a) The exploratory nature of the development of these AI systems means that the system requirements often change during development
- b) The expected behavior of these AI systems changes after the initial release with no corresponding changes to the system specification
- c) Each of these AI systems can learn in different ways, making the correctness of these systems a matter of subjective judgment
- d) The complexity of these AI systems means that manually determining their expected outputs can be especially difficult

*Select ONE answer.*

options.text: The exploratory nature of the development of these AI systems means that the system requirements often change during development
The expected behavior of these AI systems changes after the initial release with no corresponding changes to the system specification
Each of these AI systems can learn in different ways, making the correctness of these systems a matter of subjective judgment
The complexity of these AI systems means that manually determining their expected outputs can be especially difficult

rationale_units.text: Exploratory development of AI systems can often mean that the system requirements change during development, however self-learning AI systems do not have to be developed using an exploratory development approach.

Self-learning AI-based systems continuously update their internal models post-deployment. This causes the AI-based system's 'correct' behavior to change as the system evolves – and this behavior is not reflected in updated specifications.

Each self-learning AI system can learn in different ways as each will encounter different operational experiences, however this normally means that they will have slightly different expected behaviors – it does not mean that determining these expected behaviors requires subjective judgment.

Some self-learning AI systems can be complex, but that is not their defining attribute – some may be relatively simple in terms of learned behavior. Thus, there is no systemic reason that their expected outputs cannot be determined by human testers.
